question:
**Rearrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph:**

1. A central tenet of this approach is the concept of a "class," which acts as a blueprint for creating objects.

2. Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) is a programming paradigm based on the concept of "objects," which can contain data and code.

3. This allows a programmer to specify the structure and behavior of an object-oriented program.

4. The key advantage of this approach is that it models real-world entities, making complex systems easier to manage and debug.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
 
• The paragraph begins by introducing Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) as a programming paradigm based on the concept of "objects." 
 
• **Sentence 2 is the first sentence** as it provides the definition of OOP: 
 
 
• "Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) is a programming paradigm based on the concept of 'objects,' which can contain data and code." 
 
 
 
• **Sentence 1 follows** as it introduces the concept of a "class," which acts as a blueprint for creating objects: 
 
 
• "A central tenet of this approach is the concept of a 'class,' which acts as a blueprint for creating objects." 
 
 
 
• **Sentence 3 is the third sentence** as it explains how a programmer can specify the structure and behavior of an object-oriented program: 
 
 
• "This allows a programmer to specify the structure and behavior of an object-oriented program." 
 
 
 
• **Sentence 4 is the last sentence** because it highlights the key advantage of OOP: 
 
 
• "The key advantage of this approach is that it models real-world entities, making complex systems easier to manage and debug." 
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **2, 1, 3, 4**. 

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) is a programming paradigm based on the concept of 'objects,' which can contain data and code. A central tenet of this approach is the concept of a 'class,' which acts as a blueprint for creating objects. This allows a programmer to specify the structure and behavior of an object-oriented program. The key advantage of this approach is that it models real-world entities, making complex systems easier to manage and debug."</div
